electric-violet.$description: Electric Violet — Violet supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

deep-ink-violet.$description: Deep Ink Violet — Headlines, high-emphasis text, logo mark — anchors the brand without feeling heavy

heather-violet.$description: Heather Violet — Body copy, paragraph text, subdued UI labels — the workhorse text color that keeps prose warm rather than cold

mist-violet.$description: Mist Violet — Secondary text, footer labels, icon strokes, muted links — a washed violet that recedes gracefully

midnight-plum.$description: Midnight Plum — Footer background, deepest contrast surface — terminates the page with the same hue family as headings, just darker

slate-dusk.$description: Slate Dusk — Navigation text, dark-mode-leaning neutral — used where a neutral (not chromatic) dark is needed

overcast.$description: Overcast — Muted secondary text, helper copy, timestamps — the cool counterpoint to the violet body text

pure-paper.$description: Pure Paper — Card surfaces, elevated panels, button text on violet fills

lavender-mist.$description: Lavender Mist — Hairline borders, card outlines, subtle dividers, inset focus rings — the dominant structural neutral, replacing what would normally be light gray

iris-haze.$description: Iris Haze — Page background, the canvas beneath all content — a barely-perceptible lavender tint rather than pure white

dawn-wash.$description: Dawn Wash — Decorative gradient stop — sky-to-pink section bands

plum-veil.$description: Plum Veil — Supporting palette color for small decorative accents when the core palette needs contrast. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

fricolage-grotesque.$description: Body copy, UI labels, button text, navigation, footer, captions. Used at 16–18px for body and 12–15px for meta. The weight 325 light is deliberate anti-convention — most devtools use 400 minimum, this whisper weight softens the dense infrastructure copy into something editorial. Positive tracking (0.025em–0.05em) at small sizes gives uppercase labels and button text a slightly spacious, unhurried feel.

mackinac.$description: Display headlines and section titles. A high-contrast serif used at weight 500 only — the medium weight gives authority without feeling editorial-stiff. Aggressive negative tracking (-0.045em at 64px, -0.025em at 22–36px) tightens the letterspacing so the serif feels modern rather than traditional. Single most distinctive type choice on the site: pairs a humanist grotesque body with an editorial serif display to create a storybook voice.
